This article goes from FASTQ files to an `IsoformicExperiment` with transcript-level and gene-level differential expression results.
The [introduction](isoformic-introduction.html) starts one step later, from ready-made tables, and the other articles analyse the object.

## Quantifying with Salmon

We recommend [Salmon][salmon-ref] [@salmon] in selective-alignment mode against the GENCODE transcriptome, with inferential replicates so that `swish` [@swish] can be used for transcript-level differential expression.

Salmon 2 is a from-scratch rewrite in Rust (2.8.0 at the time of writing).
The workflow (`salmon index`, `salmon quant`, `quant.sf`) and the output files are the same, so `read_salmon()`, `tximeta`, `tximport` and `swish` work unchanged, but the index format is new: an index built with Salmon 1.x is rejected and must be rebuilt (the last C++ release, 1.12.0, remains available as the `salmon-cpp` conda package).
Other changes worth knowing: selective alignment is the only mapping mode (`--validateMappings` is a no-op), quantification is deterministic by default (identical output for any thread count), decoy sequences no longer appear in `quant.sf`, and `--ignoreTxVersion` matches transcript identifiers without their version suffix when a gene map is given.
The Salmon [migration guide][salmon-migration-ref] lists every removed or ignored option.

A typical single-sample invocation from a shell is below: `--libType A` detects the library type, the index is built from the GENCODE transcript FASTA with `salmon index --gencode` (which truncates the transcript names at the first `|`), `--posBias --seqBias --gcBias` correct the biases, `--dumpEq --dumpEqWeights` keep the equivalence classes and `--numGibbsSamples` writes the inferential replicates that `swish` needs into `aux_info/bootstrap/`.

``` bash
salmon index \
  --transcripts gencode.v49.transcripts.fa.gz \
  --index salmon_index \
  --gencode \
  --threads 8

salmon quant \
  --libType A \
  --index salmon_index \
  --mates1 /path/SRR..._1.fastq.gz \
  --mates2 /path/SRR..._2.fastq.gz \
  --output /path/SRR..._quant \
  --threads 8 \
  --allowDovetail --softclipOverhangs \
  --dumpEq --dumpEqWeights \
  --posBias --seqBias --gcBias \
  --numGibbsSamples 30
```

The same can be driven from R through the `condathis` package, which installs Salmon from Bioconda into a conda environment (Linux and macOS, or WSL2 on Windows).
`salmon_index()` and `salmon_quant()` run the commands above; the first call creates the environment with Salmon 2.8.0:

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(isoformic)
tx_fasta <- download_reference(version = "49", file_type = "fasta")
gff_path <- download_reference(version = "49", file_type = "gff")

salmon_index(fasta_path = tx_fasta, index_path = "salmon_index", is_gencode = TRUE, num_threads = 8)
salmon_quant(
  input_r1 = "sample_1.fastq.gz",
  input_r2 = "sample_2.fastq.gz",
  index_path = "salmon_index",
  output_dir = "quants/sample_quant",
  num_threads = 8
)
```

`salmon_quant()` draws 30 Gibbs samples per sample by default (`num_gibbs = 0` skips them).
Besides `swish`, they quantify how well the reads determine each isoform, which isoforms cannot be told apart and how confident each differential expression call is; `read_salmon(inferential = TRUE)` reads them and the [uncertainty article](isoformic-uncertainty.html) explains how to use and report them.

For a decoy-aware index (recommended by the Salmon authors), build the `gentrome` FASTA and `decoys.txt` from the genome as described in the Salmon documentation and pass `--decoys decoys.txt` to `salmon index`.

## Reading quantifications directly

`read_salmon()` reads any number of `quant.sf` files with DuckDB and returns an `IsoformicExperiment` with `abundance` (TPM), `counts` and `length` assays.
The package ships a down-sampled dataset of six placenta samples quantified against GENCODE v49.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(isoformic)

quants_dir <- fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata", "mini_quants")
quant_dirs <- fs::dir_ls(quants_dir, type = "directory")
names(quant_dirs) <- sub("_quant$", "", fs::path_file(quant_dirs))

col_data <- tibble::tibble(
  sample_id = names(quant_dirs),
  condition = factor(c(rep("control", 3), rep("treatment", 3)), levels = c("control", "treatment"))
)
col_data
```

The annotation must match the reference used for quantification, GENCODE v49 here.
For real data it is downloaded once into the package cache and converted to Parquet once:

```{r}
#| eval: false
gff_path <- download_reference(version = "49", file_type = "gff")
annot_dir <- prepare_isoformic_annotation(gff_path)
```

The package bundles the subset of that annotation covering the transcripts of the mini dataset.

```{r}
annot_dir <- fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata", "mini_annotation")

iso <- read_salmon(quant_dirs, annot_path = annot_dir, col_data = col_data, experiment_name = "mini_placenta")
iso
assay_names(iso)
head(row_data(iso))
```

## Transcript-level differential expression with swish

`swish` needs the inferential replicates, which `tximeta` imports from the Salmon output (the bundled quantifications carry them separately to keep the package small).

```{r}
#| message: false
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(SummarizedExperiment)
  library(fishpond)
})

tximeta_coldata <- data.frame(
  files = fs::path(quant_dirs, "quant.sf"),
  names = names(quant_dirs),
  condition = col_data$condition
)
se_tx <- tximeta::tximeta(
  coldata = tximeta_coldata,
  type = "salmon",
  txOut = TRUE,
  skipMeta = TRUE,
  useHub = FALSE,
  ignoreAfterBar = TRUE,
  skipSeqinfo = TRUE
)
mini_draws <- as_inferential_replicates(
  read_parquet(fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata", "mini_draws.parquet"))
)
names(mini_draws) <- paste0("infRep", seq_along(mini_draws))
assays(se_tx) <- c(as.list(assays(se_tx)), mini_draws)

y <- fishpond::scaleInfReps(se_tx)
y <- fishpond::labelKeep(y, minCount = 10, minN = 3)
set.seed(20261029) # swish uses permutations
y <- fishpond::swish(y, x = "condition")

swish_results <- mcols(y) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("transcript_id")
head(swish_results)
```

The results are attached to the object; `tximeta` objects can also be converted directly with `as_isoformic(se_tx, annot_path = annot_dir)`.

```{r}
de_tx(iso) <- swish_results
head(de_tx(iso))
```

## Gene-level differential expression with DESeq2

`as_summarized_experiment()` exports the gene-level assays (isoforms summed, lengths averaged by abundance) so that `DESeq2` can run on them.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
se_gene <- as_summarized_experiment(iso, level = "gene")
assay(se_gene, "counts") <- round(assay(se_gene, "counts"))
se_gene$condition <- factor(se_gene$condition, levels = c("control", "treatment"))

dds <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSet(se_gene, design = ~condition)
dds <- dds[rowSums(DESeq2::counts(dds) >= 10) >= 3, ]
dds <- DESeq2::DESeq(dds, quiet = TRUE)
res <- DESeq2::results(dds, contrast = c("condition", "treatment", "control"))
shrink_type <- if (rlang::is_installed("apeglm")) "apeglm" else "normal"
res_shr <- DESeq2::lfcShrink(dds, coef = "condition_treatment_vs_control", res = res, type = shrink_type, quiet = TRUE)

de_gene(iso) <- as.data.frame(res_shr)
head(de_gene(iso))
iso
```

## Looking at the results

```{r}
top_gene <- de_gene(iso) |>
  dplyr::arrange(qvalue) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 1) |>
  dplyr::pull(gene_id)
gene_name <- gene_data(iso)$gene_name[gene_data(iso)$gene_id == top_gene]
gene_name

plot_log2fc(iso, feature = gene_name)
plot_tx_expr(iso, gene_name = gene_name, group = "condition")
plot_genomic_context(iso, gene_name = gene_name)
isoform_switches(iso) |> head()
```

## Saving

The object, with both result tables, is written as a directory of Parquet files and restored with `read_isoformic()`.

```{r}
out_dir <- fs::path(tempdir(), "mini_placenta")
iso <- write_isoformic(iso, out_dir, overwrite = TRUE)
iso@data_path
fs::dir_ls(out_dir)
```

## Long reads with Oarfish

Oxford Nanopore and PacBio reads are quantified with Oarfish, which writes bootstrap replicates and a table of unique and shared reads next to the counts.
`read_oarfish()` reads them like `read_salmon()` and the uncertainty functions of the [uncertainty article](isoformic-uncertainty.html) work on them unchanged.
The three samples below are simulated nanopore reads of the RBPJ transcripts, quantified with Oarfish 0.10.3 and 30 bootstrap replicates (`data-raw/oarfish/`), so they only show the file layout and the functions, not a real library.

```{r}
oarfish_dir <- fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata", "oarfish")
prefixes <- fs::path(oarfish_dir, c("control_1", "control_2", "treated_1"))
names(prefixes) <- fs::path_file(prefixes)
fs::dir_ls(oarfish_dir, regexp = "treated_1")

iso_long <- read_oarfish(
  prefixes,
  annot_path = fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata", "example_experiment", "annotation"),
  inferential = TRUE
)
iso_long
tx_uncertainty(iso_long) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(mean_inf_rv)) |>
  dplyr::select(transcript_name, mean_count, mean_inf_rv, unique_fraction) |>
  head(6)
```

The Oarfish output has no TPM, so the `abundance` assay is computed from the read counts and the transcript lengths.
`unique_fraction` comes from the unique and shared read counts of `.ambig_info.tsv`; Oarfish has no equivalence classes, so `n_classes` is not available.
Samples quantified by Oarfish and by Salmon cannot be read together.

In single-cell mode (`--single-cell`, on a transcriptome-aligned BAM whose reads carry their cell barcode in the `CB:Z` tag) Oarfish writes a cell by transcript count matrix and no replicates.
`read_oarfish_sc()` sums the cells of each sample, given a table of barcodes and samples, so the isoform analyses apply to samples or to cell types (give each combination of sample and cell type its own `sample_id`).
The example has 60 simulated cells in three samples:

```{r}
sc_dir <- fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata", "oarfish_sc")
cells <- read.delim(fs::path(sc_dir, "cells.tsv"))
head(cells, 3)
iso_sc <- read_oarfish_sc(
  fs::path(sc_dir, "out"),
  cells = cells,
  annot_path = fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata", "example_experiment", "annotation")
)
col_data(iso_sc)
```

## Next steps

From here the object is analysed like the one of the introduction: [transcriptomic diversity](isoformic-diversity.html), [isoform structure and productivity](isoformic-productivity.html), [alternative polyadenylation](isoformic-polyadenylation.html), [enrichment by transcript type](isoformic-enrichment.html) and [plots](isoformic-plots.html).
The inferential replicates imported above can be stored in `metadata(iso)$inf_reps` so that `productive_fraction()` reports the uncertainty of each fraction.
